name: Seville Cathedral
places: Patio de los Naranjos, Seville Cathedral
description: A vast Gothic cathedral built on the site of a mosque. The mosque’s minaret became the Giralda bell tower, and its orange-tree courtyard survives.

name: Archive of the Indies
places: General Archive of the Indies (Archivo de Indias)
description: A 16th-century merchants’ exchange next to the cathedral, now holding the records of Spain’s empire in the Americas. Some rooms are open to visitors.

name: Real Alcázar
description: A royal palace begun in the Middle Ages, with Mudéjar halls, tiled courtyards and large gardens. The upper floors are still used by the Spanish royal family.

name: Plaza Nueva
description: A large open square by the city hall, with a statue of King Ferdinand III on horseback in the middle.

name: Alameda de Hércules
description: A long tree-lined promenade laid out in the 1500s, with old stone columns at each end, now lined with bars and busy at night.

name: Torre del Oro
description: A 13th-century Moorish watchtower on the riverbank, built to guard the port. Inside is a small naval museum, with views from the top.

name: Maestranza bullring
description: An 18th-century bullring by the river, one of the oldest in Spain, with a museum and guided tours.

name: Triana Bridge
description: A 19th-century iron bridge over the Guadalquivir, linking the centre with Triana, the old potters’ and flamenco quarter.

name: Royal Tobacco Factory
description: A huge 18th-century tobacco factory, now part of the university. Carmen, the heroine of Bizet’s opera, works here as a cigar-maker.

name: Hospital de la Caridad
description: A 17th-century almshouse near the river, still caring for the elderly, with a baroque church full of paintings by Murillo and Valdés Leal.
